communications.subject: California Public Records Act Request: Untitled
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the California Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

Dear Ventura County Public Records Coordinator:
Pursuant to the California Public Records Act, Government Code § 7920.000 et seq., I request copies of public records concerning Ventura County and the Ventura County Sheriff's Office (“VCSO”) acquisition, installation, operation, administration, use, oversight, and sharing of information obtained through Flock Safety automated license plate recognition (“ALPR”) cameras and related Flock Safety technology.

For purposes of this request, “Flock/ALPR information” includes information collected through Flock Safety cameras, ALPR systems, Flock Safety software and databases, and any related vehicle-location, license-plate, vehicle-characteristic, alert, or investigative information.

This request includes Flock/ALPR systems operated, owned, leased, funded, administered, or otherwise controlled by Ventura County or VCSO, including systems located in unincorporated areas of the County, County Service Areas, and other areas where the County or VCSO has responsibility for or access to the system.
It also includes records concerning Ventura County's or VCSO's access to Flock systems or Flock/ALPR information maintained by another governmental agency, private entity, municipality, school, business, neighborhood organization, or other third party.
1. Contracts, agreements, and financial records
All contracts, agreements, memoranda of understanding, purchase orders, invoices, amendments, renewals, extensions, proposals, quotes, statements of work, and other agreements between Ventura County, VCSO, or any County department and Flock Group, Inc., Flock Safety, or any related Flock entity.
All records concerning the County's initial acquisition or implementation of Flock Safety ALPR technology, including Board of Supervisors agenda materials, staff reports, recommendations, presentations, resolutions, approvals, and related documentation.
All records concerning the acquisition or implementation of Flock cameras through County Service Areas, Municipal Advisory Councils, grant-funded programs, Sheriff's Office programs, or other County-administered programs.
All records reflecting the total cost of the Flock program, including installation, equipment, software, licensing, subscriptions, maintenance, replacement, upgrades, cellular/data service, storage, and other associated costs.
All invoices and payment records relating to Flock Safety from the beginning of the County's relationship with Flock through the date this request is processed.
All records concerning grants, state or federal funding, donations, private funding, County Service Area funds, or other sources used to acquire or operate Flock cameras.
All records concerning any proposal, quote, bid, solicitation, procurement, or competitive process relating to the acquisition of Flock technology.
2. Number, location, and operation of cameras
Records identifying the total number of Flock Safety ALPR cameras currently operated, owned, leased, funded, or otherwise controlled by Ventura County or VCSO.
Records identifying the location of each Flock camera, including installation addresses, intersections, street locations, geographic coordinates, or other location information sufficient to identify where each camera is installed.
Records identifying the date each camera was installed, activated, deactivated, relocated, replaced, or removed.
Records identifying the type and model of each Flock camera or device currently or previously deployed by Ventura County or VCSO.
Records identifying which cameras are located within incorporated municipalities but are accessible by, operated by, funded by, or otherwise connected to Ventura County or VCSO.
Records concerning any proposed expansion, reduction, relocation, replacement, or modification of the County's Flock camera network.
3. Policies, procedures, and legal authority
The County's and VCSO's current and all prior Flock Safety/ALPR usage and privacy policies.
All policies, directives, general orders, standard operating procedures, training materials, manuals, instructions, or other documents governing the access, search, use, retention, sharing, dissemination, or deletion of Flock/ALPR information.
All records identifying the County official, Sheriff, employee, unit, or other person responsible for custody, administration, oversight, or implementation of the County's Flock/ALPR information.
All records identifying the job classifications, positions, units, employees, contractors, or other persons authorized to access Flock/ALPR information.
All records concerning training required or provided to personnel who have access to Flock/ALPR information, including privacy, civil liberties, data security, ALPR operation, appropriate-use, and data-sharing training.
All legal opinions, memoranda, analyses, correspondence, or other records concerning the legality or constitutionality of the County's or VCSO's use of Flock Safety ALPR technology.
All records concerning compliance with California Civil Code §§ 1798.90.5–1798.90.55 and any other applicable California or federal law governing ALPR technology or surveillance systems.
4. Board of Supervisors, public approval, and public notice
All Ventura County Board of Supervisors agenda packets, staff reports, presentations, minutes, recordings, resolutions, ordinances, notices, and other records concerning the County's decision to implement, continue, expand, renew, or modify its Flock ALPR program.
All records concerning public meetings of the Board of Supervisors, Municipal Advisory Councils, County Service Areas, or other County bodies at which Flock Safety or ALPR technology was discussed.
All records concerning opportunities provided to the public to comment on implementation or operation of the County's ALPR program.
All records identifying the date and meeting at which the governing body provided or considered public comment concerning implementation of the ALPR system.
All correspondence received from members of the public concerning Flock Safety or the County's ALPR program.
5. ALPR searches and access
Records sufficient to show the number of searches or queries conducted through the County's Flock system, broken down by month, from the beginning of the program through the date this request is processed.
Records sufficient to show the number of Flock/ALPR searches conducted by each authorized user, employee, unit, department, or agency, to the extent such information is maintained.
Records of access to ALPR information maintained pursuant to California Civil Code § 1798.90.52, including the date and time of access, query terms or data elements used, username or identifying information of the person conducting the search, affiliated organization, and stated purpose for the search.
Records concerning audits, reviews, investigations, or monitoring of employee or contractor access to Flock/ALPR information.
All records concerning any unauthorized, improper, excessive, or suspected misuse of the Flock/ALPR system or its data.
All records concerning complaints, disciplinary actions, investigations, or corrective actions involving improper access or use of Flock/ALPR information.
6. Data retention and deletion
Records establishing the County's current retention period for Flock/ALPR information.
All policies, procedures, technical settings, contractual provisions, or other records governing the retention and deletion of Flock/ALPR information.
Records sufficient to establish whether Flock/ALPR data is automatically deleted after a specified period and, if so, the applicable retention period.
Records concerning any exceptions to the County's standard retention period, including circumstances in which data is retained because it is associated with an investigation, criminal case, evidence, warrant, subpoena, litigation hold, or other legal purpose.
Records sufficient to show the volume or amount of ALPR data retained by the County, if such records are maintained.
7. Data sharing and outside access
All records concerning Ventura County's or VCSO's participation in any Flock Safety national, regional, statewide, or multi-agency data-sharing network.
All agreements, memoranda, policies, authorizations, correspondence, or other records concerning sharing of Ventura County or VCSO Flock/ALPR data with other law enforcement agencies or public agencies.
Records identifying every outside agency, department, task force, or governmental entity that has been granted access to Ventura County or VCSO Flock/ALPR data or with which Ventura County or VCSO has shared such information.
Records concerning any access by outside agencies to Ventura County or VCSO Flock/ALPR data, including records sufficient to identify the agency, date, purpose, and type of access, to the extent maintained.
Records concerning any requests by outside agencies for Ventura County or VCSO Flock/ALPR information.
All records concerning any sharing, transfer, disclosure, or access to Flock/ALPR information by federal law-enforcement agencies or federal governmental entities, including but not limited to U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), Customs and Border Protection (CBP), Homeland Security Investigations (HSI), the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), or any federal task force.
All records concerning whether Ventura County or VCSO has enabled, disabled, accepted, rejected, or otherwise participated in any Flock Safety national database or nationwide data-sharing functionality.
All records concerning any requests for or access to Ventura County or VCSO Flock/ALPR information relating to immigration enforcement, immigration investigations, reproductive healthcare, political activity, protests, demonstrations, or other constitutionally protected activity.
8. Flock Community Network and privately owned cameras
All records concerning the County's or VCSO's use of or participation in Flock Safety's Community Network Access or any substantially similar Flock feature.
Records identifying privately owned Flock cameras, including cameras operated by businesses, homeowners' associations, schools, neighborhood organizations, or other private entities, to which County or VCSO personnel have direct or indirect access.
All agreements, authorizations, policies, correspondence, or other records concerning the County's or VCSO's ability to request or obtain access to privately owned Flock camera feeds or Flock-generated information.
Records sufficient to identify the number of requests made by County or VCSO personnel for access to privately owned Flock cameras or feeds.
Records sufficient to identify the number of privately owned Flock cameras or camera feeds available to County or VCSO personnel through the Flock platform.
Records concerning whether privately owned Flock cameras are included in any County or VCSO searchable database, map, network, or investigative platform.
9. Flock Safety system capabilities and configuration
All records describing the capabilities and functions enabled on the County's Flock system, including the types of vehicle information, license plate information, vehicle characteristics, location information, images, alerts, or other data collected.
Records identifying which Flock Safety products, modules, software features, databases, or services are enabled for Ventura County or VCSO.
Records concerning use or availability of Flock's vehicle search, vehicle fingerprinting, hot-list, alert, sharing, analytics, or other investigative functions.
Records concerning any integration between Flock Safety and other County or law-enforcement systems, databases, records-management systems, computer-aided dispatch systems, camera systems, or investigative platforms.
Records concerning any use of Flock data in connection with facial recognition, biometric identification, person identification, predictive policing, artificial intelligence, or other automated analytical technology.
Records concerning Flock's Vehicle Fingerprint or similar vehicle-identification technology as configured or used by Ventura County or VCSO.
Records concerning automated alerts generated through Flock, including alerts associated with NCIC, NCMEC, hot lists, stolen vehicles, wanted persons, missing persons, or other databases.
10. Effectiveness and results
All reports, statistics, analyses, presentations, or evaluations concerning the effectiveness of the County's Flock program.
Records sufficient to identify crimes, arrests, citations, stolen-vehicle recoveries, missing-person recoveries, investigations, prosecutions, or other law-enforcement outcomes that the County or VCSO attributes to information obtained through Flock/ALPR technology.
Any cost-benefit analyses, performance evaluations, return-on-investment analyses, or assessments of whether Flock cameras have achieved the County's stated objectives.
Any reports or records concerning false alerts, inaccurate plate reads, misidentification, system errors, or other reliability issues involving Flock technology.
Records concerning instances in which Flock information was used to initiate, support, or materially advance an investigation, arrest, search warrant, surveillance activity, or other law-enforcement action.
11. Security and data breaches
All records concerning cybersecurity incidents, vulnerabilities, unauthorized access, data breaches, system compromises, or other security incidents involving the County's Flock system or Flock/ALPR data.
All notices, reports, correspondence, investigations, or assessments concerning any actual or suspected unauthorized disclosure or access to Flock/ALPR information.
Records concerning security audits, penetration testing, vulnerability assessments, or other security assessments of the Flock system, to the extent such records are not exempt from disclosure.
12. Communications concerning Flock
All emails, memoranda, letters, text messages maintained as public records, meeting notes, and other correspondence between County/VCSO officials or employees and Flock Safety representatives concerning the County's Flock program.
All communications between County/VCSO officials or employees and other governmental agencies concerning Flock Safety, ALPR technology, data sharing, privacy, retention, surveillance, or related issues.
All communications concerning concerns, complaints, objections, privacy issues, civil-liberties issues, or legal issues relating to Flock Safety or the County's ALPR program.
All communications between Flock Safety and the Ventura County Sheriff's Office concerning access to, sharing of, or searches of Flock data maintained by other law-enforcement agencies.
13. Grant-funded cameras and County Service Areas
All records concerning the acquisition, funding, installation, operation, and maintenance of Flock cameras using state, federal, County Service Area, or other grant funding.
All grant applications, grant awards, grant agreements, reimbursement requests, grant reports, and grant-related correspondence concerning Flock Safety cameras.
All records concerning the three Flock license plate readers reported as approved and installed in Oak Park, including records concerning their funding, installation, ownership, operation, maintenance, data retention, and access.
All records concerning any Flock cameras proposed, approved, funded, or installed in Oak Park, Oak View, or any other unincorporated Ventura County community.
All records identifying the governmental entity or department that owns the cameras and the governmental entity or department responsible for the data generated by those cameras.
14. Current status
Records sufficient to establish whether Ventura County and/or VCSO currently intends to continue operating the Flock Safety ALPR program.
All records concerning any proposed renewal, amendment, expansion, termination, suspension, or replacement of the County's Flock Safety contract or program.
Any current Flock Safety contract, renewal agreement, amendment, or other document establishing the County's present contractual relationship with Flock.
Records concerning any change to the County's Flock program, privacy policy, data-sharing practices, retention period, or access permissions since January 1, 2026.
Request for electronic production
Please provide responsive records electronically in their native electronic format where reasonably available, including searchable PDF, Excel/CSV, or other native formats for databases, spreadsheets, logs, and reports.
For records that exist in a database or other electronic system, I request an electronic export of the responsive data rather than screenshots or summaries, where reasonably practicable.
For access logs, audit logs, query logs, event logs, hot-list reports, and similar electronic records, please provide the underlying electronic records in a machine-readable format where reasonably available.
I am requesting existing records and am not asking the County to create a new record or answer questions. Where a requested record is maintained in a database or other electronic system that can reasonably be queried or exported, please provide the resulting electronic record to the extent permitted by the California Public Records Act.
Segregation of exempt information
If the County believes any responsive record contains information exempt from disclosure, please provide all reasonably segregable portions of the record after redacting only the information specifically exempt from disclosure, pursuant to Government Code § 7922.525.
If any portion of this request is denied, please identify the specific statutory exemption relied upon for each withheld record or portion thereof and provide the factual basis for the claimed exemption. Please also identify the name and title/position of each person responsible for the denial, as required by Government Code § 7922.540.
If the County contends that records are exempt under the California Constitution, Government Code, Evidence Code, Penal Code, Civil Code, or any other statute, please identify the specific statutory provision relied upon.
If records are withheld pursuant to the catch-all exemption or another balancing test, please provide the County's specific justification demonstrating why the public interest served by withholding the records clearly outweighs the public interest served by disclosure.
Search and response
Please construe this request broadly to include records maintained by:
• Ventura County Sheriff's Office
• Ventura County Executive Office
• Ventura County Board of Supervisors
• County Counsel
• County Information Technology Services
• County Procurement/General Services
• County Auditor-Controller/Treasurer-Tax Collector, where applicable
• County Service Areas
• Sheriff's Office command staff
• Sheriff's Office investigations/divisions
• Any other County department, division, unit, employee, contractor, or agent reasonably likely to possess responsive records
Please also include responsive records maintained on behalf of the County by Flock Safety or another contractor to the extent those records constitute public records subject to disclosure.
If responsive records are maintained by VCSO rather than the County's central records system, please treat this request as applying to both entities and route the request accordingly rather than requiring a new request.
If the County believes this request is overly broad or requires clarification, please contact me promptly and identify the specific portion that requires clarification rather than denying the request in its entirety.
I request that the County comply with the California Public Records Act's applicable response deadlines, including Government Code § 7922.535.
If responsive records are available on an existing County website, please provide the direct location of those records; however, I request electronic copies of records that are not readily accessible online.
Please preserve all potentially responsive records while this request is pending.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 calendar days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Juiciest

title: ForwardEdge ASIC (City of Saint Paul, Minnesota - City Attorney)

communications.subject: Minnesota Government Data Practices Act Request: ForwardEdge ASIC (City of Saint Paul, Minnesota - City Attorney)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Minnesota Government Data Practices Act, I hereby request the following records:

I am requesting any records and documents and communications that pertain to or reference the company ForwardEdge ASIC located at 2340 Energy Park Drive, St Paul. This request also encompasses documents and records from any of ForwardEdge’s parent and subsidiary entities, to the extent they relate to any request below.
My request encompasses any documents and city communications which name ForwardEdge ASIC, including but not limited to:
(a) reports, slide decks, presentations, documents, or communications from ForwardEdge ASIC to the City of St. Paul (“the City”) regarding or referring to the Minnesota Investment Fund (“MIF”) loan
(b) any contracts signed between ForwardEdge ASIC, or any entity on behalf of ForwardEdge ASIC, and the City
(c) any loan provided by the City to ForwardEdge ASIC, or any entity on behalf of ForwardEdge ASIC, and any related reporting requirements the City imposed on the recipient
(d) any grant applications and grant application materials submitted to the City of St Paul by ForwardEdge ASIC, or any entity on behalf of ForwardEdge ASIC, for the MIF loan
(e) any other applications that ForwardEdge ASIC has submitted to the City,
(f) records that show how much of the MIF loan funds have been dispersed as of the date of this request, and any expected distributions in the year 2026
(g) any other documents that refer to ForwardEdge ASIC.
(h) any communications between the city of Saint Paul and the Saint Paul Police Department regarding ForwardEdge ASIC.
(h) any email communications between ForwardEdge ASIC, on any entity on behalf of ForwardEdge ASIC, and the City between April 24, 2025 and Jul 13, 2026.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days.

Sincerely,

Arco Orca

communications.subject: The Missouri Sunshine Law Request: ALPR audit
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the The Missouri Sunshine Law, I hereby request the following records:

Concerning Flock Safety, these files;

1. Organization Audit in Flock.
The report should include data logged from the period of January 1, 2025, to the date this request is processed. Per Flock's documentation, the Organization Audit is available within the Insights tab and is defined as searches done within the agency.

2. Network Audit in Flock.
The report should include data logged from the period of January 1, 2025, to the date this request is processed. Per Flock's documentation, the Network Audit is available within the Insights tab and is defined as searches of the organization’s Flock network by any agency in the Flock System.

Typically the output for these audits is available in monthly batches.

3. A list of network share settings that include:
3a. Flock networks shared with me
3b. Networks that I’m sharing

Please provide records in their original electronic, machine readable format. For example, please provide csv or spreadsheet files where applicable.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 3 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Kansas City DSA

title: (WA ESD 123) All Emails Sent to or Received from mcminimeelaw.com

communications.subject: Washington Public Records Act Request: (WA ESD 123) All Emails Sent to or Received from mcminimeelaw.com
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Washington Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

All electronic mail sent to or received from any email address operating under
the domain "mcminimeelaw.com" (matching the wildcard string *@mcminimeelaw.com)
exchanged with any district email account, alias, or internal
routing node, acting as either the author, sender, primary recipient,
carbon copy (CC), or blind carbon copy (BCC) holder.

The chronological scope of this request spans the entirety of the District's
available archival retention window.

TECHNICAL PRE-EXCLUSION OF REPETITIVE SYSTEM DATA:

To maximize administrative processing efficiency, accelerate delivery, and
eliminate unnecessary review burdens, the requester explicitly waives
interest in, pre-excludes, and requests the system-level filtering out of
the following non-substantive records categories:

1. Automated calendar invitations, change notifications, or updates.
2. Automated out-of-office or vacation autoreplies generated by either domain.
3. System-generated IT alerts, ticket confirmations, or password actions.

LIMITATION OF SCOPE & PRE-EXCLUSION OF SENSITIVE DATA:

The requester explicitly pre-excludes and waives any interest in the
Personally Identifiable Information (PII) of any individual student under FERPA.

Pursuant to RCW 42.56.210, if the District asserts that specific internal
staff names or student indicators are exempt from disclosure, the District is
required to apply narrow blackouts exclusively to those individual text strings
while releasing the remaining non-exempt text blocks, financial totals,
and generalized policy or administrative discussions.

Blanket withholding of entire records based on broad assertions of privilege
or exempt status is explicitly contested; only the minimal exempt portions
may be withheld.

MANDATORY STATUTORY COMPLIANCE TIMELINE:

As provided by RCW 42.56.520, a formal response is required within five (5)
business days.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 5 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Public Interest Mainstreaming Parenting

title: Entergy Lawsuit v. Arkansas Democrat-Gazette

communications.subject: Arkansas Freedom of Information Act Request: Entergy Lawsuit v. Arkansas Democrat-Gazette
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Arkansas Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

1. Any communications to or from Entergy, Entergy Arkansas, or its representatives (including Wright, Lindsey & Jennings LLP,  Stephen R. Lancaster, and Gary D. Marts, Jr.) between August 30, 2026 and September 4, 2026.

2. Any communications to or from the Office of the Executive Director (between August 30, 2026, and September 4, 2026) containing any of the following terms: "Altitude Capital", "Cypress Solar", "data center", "EAL", "Entergy", "Arkansas Times", "Kivell", "Sasser", "Democrat", "Gazette", "Democrat-Gazette", "ADG", "Byron Tate", "TRO", or "Temporary Restraining Order".

3. Any communications or other records concerning the lawsuit filed by Entergy Arkansas, filed as Entergy Arkansas, LLC v. Arkansas Democrat-Gazette, Inc. (No. 4:25-cv-899) in the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Arkansas.

4. Any communications or other records concerning the release of information in response to a FOIA request by Jessica Kivell.

5. A copy of any FOIA request by Jessica Kivell since January 1, 2026.

"COMMUNICATIONS" means any transmission or exchange of information, whether incoming, outgoing, internal, or external, including emails and attachments; text messages, including SMS, MMS, and iMessage; messages sent through Signal, WhatsApp, or similar applications; messages sent through Microsoft Teams, Slack, Google Chat, or other collaboration platforms; direct or group messages on social-media platforms; letters and memoranda; shared documents and comments; calendar invitations and entries; meeting notices, agendas, notes, and minutes; telephone and videoconference records; call logs; voicemail messages; reactions; forwarded content; and associated metadata. 

This request includes responsive records concerning official business regardless of the account, device, platform, server, network, or storage location on which they were created, sent, received, maintained, or stored. This includes responsive records in personal or non-government email accounts, messaging accounts, social-media accounts, cloud-storage accounts, computers, or mobile devices, to the extent those records are within the agency's possession, custody, or control or are otherwise subject to disclosure under applicable law. The agency should instruct each custodian reasonably likely to possess responsive records to search any personal or non-government account, application, or device used to conduct official business and to provide any responsive records to the agency for processing. The use of a personal account, application, or device does not exclude an otherwise responsive official-business record from the scope of this request.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 3 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Adam Steinbaugh

title: SJPD ALPR audits 2024–2025, annual data usage reports, and personal-device / off-duty access rules

communications.subject: California Public Records Act Request: SJPD ALPR audits 2024–2025, annual data usage reports, and personal-device / off-duty access rules
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the California Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

1. Each audit of Department use of the Flock automated license plate reader (ALPR) system that covers any search conducted from January 1, 2024 through April 30, 2025, including any monthly audit and any periodic, random audit conducted under the Accountability provisions of Duty Manual section L 4207: each audit report or memorandum, worksheet, checklist, and list of searches sampled or flagged, and any record of the finding or corrective action for each flagged search.

2. The internal search history audit of the Flock ALPR system (organization audit) for calendar year 2025 conducted on February 4, 2026, as described in the Chief's February 9, 2026 memorandum "Automated License Plate Readers Data Usage Protocol Update" (File No. 26-215): the audit report, worksheet, criteria applied, and any list of searches examined or flagged. Also any comparable audit of calendar year 2024 search history.

3. The Department's annual ALPR data usage reports for calendar years 2024 and 2025, as submitted, including their audit narratives.

4. The memorandum or directive issued in or about September 2026 restricting access to law enforcement databases from personal electronic devices; any earlier policy change restricting access to ALPR or other law enforcement sensitive systems from personal devices; and any written policy, directive, order, or training material in effect at any time from January 1, 2024 until that memorandum that addresses access to the Flock ALPR system, or to Department law enforcement databases generally, from a personal device or while off duty.

This request does not seek internal affairs or personnel investigation records.

Duty Manual section L 4207 provides that "[a]udit trails shall be maintained by the Department for a minimum of two (2) years." Some of the period covered by this request is at or near that minimum, so I ask that the audit records responsive to this request, and the audit trails they reviewed, be preserved while it is pending.

If any record or portion of a record is withheld, please identify the exemption asserted for it and release any reasonably segregable portion. Please produce records for each item as they become available rather than holding the request for the slowest item. I request electronic copies.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

title: Prescott AZ Flock Safety Organizational Audit

communications.subject: Arizona Public Records Law Request: Prescott AZ Flock Safety Organizational Audit
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Arizona Public Records Law, I hereby request the following records:

I am requesting a copy of the following record related to your agency's use of Flock Safety surveillance systems (including automated license plate reader, or "ALPR," cameras):

Organization Audit Log, for the period of August 31, 2025 through August 31, 2026

Specifically, I am requesting the log of license plate and other searches performed by your agency's own operators (the Flock "Organization Audit Log"), for the period of August 31, 2025 through August 31, 2026, including operator names, license plates searched, search reasons, case numbers, filters, camera counts, search time frames, search type, text prompts, and moderation fields. 

This record can be exported from the Flock software's "Insights" section as a CSV file. Per Flock Safety's own "Guide to Flock Safety Data for Open Records Laws" (Sept. 3, 2025): "The audit logs can be accessed via your agency's Flock admin dashboard on the 'Insights' tab.... Customers may download these logs in the user interface as spreadsheets in 31-day increments. It is recommended that Flock customer support assist customers with the downloads when feasible for timeframes larger than six months and major accounts." (Flock Safety, Guide to Flock Safety Data for Open Records Laws, Sept. 3, 2025.) Please provide the record in its original electronic format (CSV or Excel) where possible. I have attached a screenshot from a Flock presentation on how the admin can access this.

Under Arizona's Public Records Law, A.R.S. §§ 39-121 through 39-121.03, public records in the custody of a state or local government officer must be made available for inspection and copying, and the custodian must respond promptly. A.R.S. § 39-121.01(D)(1) requires the custodian to "promptly" furnish copies of the record. Arizona courts have defined "prompt" as "quick to act... done, spoken, etc. at once or without delay," and have held the agency bears the burden of proving its response was prompt given the circumstances (West Valley View, Inc. v. Maricopa County Sheriff's Office, 216 Ariz. 225, 230, ¶ 21, 165 P.3d 203, 208 (App. 2007)); an agency that delays delivery without legal justification wrongfully denies the request (Phoenix New Times, L.L.C. v. Arpaio, 217 Ariz. 533, 547, ¶ 49, 177 P.3d 275, 289 (App. 2008)). Please confirm receipt of this request within a reasonably prompt period — no more than a few business days — and provide the record, a fee estimate, or the specific statutory basis for any withholding.

If any portion of this record is withheld, please identify the specific statutory exemption relied upon for each withheld field or row, rather than withholding the record in full; Arizona law requires the agency to segregate and disclose the non-exempt portions of a record rather than deny the request wholesale (Star Publishing Co. v. Pima County Attorney's Office, 181 Ariz. 432, 891 P.2d 899 (App. 1994)). If fees are anticipated, please provide an itemized estimate and the legal authority for each charge before incurring them.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days.

Sincerely,

Jason Hunyar

I understand this record is typically exported with operator names and plates redacted with asterisks by Flock's own software; I am not asking your agency to manually redact beyond what the system itself provides. Please produce the record as it is generated by the Flock "Insights" export. I have attached a screenshot from a Flock presentation on how the admin can access this. Please note that some files might have to be exported in multiple segments per month because of excel's row limit. This record can be exported from the Flock software's "Insights" section as a CSV file. Per Flock Safety's own "Guide to Flock Safety Data for Open Records Laws" (Sept. 3, 2025): "The audit logs can be accessed via your agency's Flock admin dashboard on the 'Insights' tab.... Customers may download these logs in the user interface as spreadsheets in 31-day increments. It is recommended that Flock customer support assist customers with the downloads when feasible for timeframes larger than six months and major accounts." (Flock Safety, Guide to Flock Safety Data for Open Records Laws, Sept. 3, 2025.) Please provide the record in its original electronic format (CSV or Excel) where possible. Under Arizona's Public Records Law, A.R.S. §§ 39-121 through 39-121.03, public records in the custody of a state or local government officer must be made available for inspection and copying, and the custodian must respond promptly. A.R.S. § 39-121.01(D)(1) requires the custodian to "promptly" furnish copies of the record. Arizona courts have defined "prompt" as "quick to act... done, spoken, etc. at once or without delay," and have held the agency bears the burden of proving its response was prompt given the circumstances (West Valley View, Inc. v. Maricopa County Sheriff's Office, 216 Ariz. 225, 230, ¶ 21, 165 P.3d 203, 208 (App. 2007)); an agency that delays delivery without legal justification wrongfully denies the request (Phoenix New Times, L.L.C. v. Arpaio, 217 Ariz. 533, 547, ¶ 49, 177 P.3d 275, 289 (App. 2008)). Pima County Attorney's Office, 181 Ariz. 432, 891 P.2d 899 (App. 1994)). If fees are anticipated, please provide an itemized estimate and the legal authority for each charge before incurring them. title: Flock Safety ALPR Records (Contracts, Audit Logs, SB 34, Communications)

communications.subject: California Public Records Act Request: Flock Safety ALPR Records (Contracts, Audit Logs, SB 34, Communications)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the California Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

Pursuant to the California Public Records Act, I request the following records concerning any products, services, platforms, sensors, or data feeds of the following categories, whether currently used, previously used, piloted, trialed, or formally considered by this agency, for the period January 1, 2020 through August 19, 2026:

Automated license plate reader ("ALPR") and connected-camera systems — including but not limited to Flock Safety (Flock Group Inc.), Motorola Solutions / Vigilant Solutions (LEARN, PlateSearch), Genetec (AutoVu), Axon / Fusus, Rekor, Leonardo/ELSAG, Neology, and Digital Recognition Network (DRN);
Data-integration, analytics, and "real-time crime center" (RTCC) / "real-time awareness center" (RTAC) platforms — including but not limited to Peregrine Technologies (peregrine.io), Palantir, Fusus (Axon), SoundThinking, and any comparable platform that aggregates, links, or searches across agency data sources; and
Any product beyond ALPR cameras offered by the above vendors (e.g., Flock's Condor PTZ video, FlockOS, Nova, or other data-intelligence products; Peregrine's data-integration or AI/"safety flagging" modules).

Where a term below refers to a Flock-specific feature (e.g., "Organization Audit"), please read it to also request the equivalent record in any other vendor's system.
1. Contracts and procurement. All contracts, master services agreements, order forms, amendments, renewals, statements of work, quotes, proposals, purchase orders, invoices, and payment records with any vendor identified above, including any data-processing addenda / data-processing agreements (DPAs), memoranda of understanding (MOUs), and any competitive-bid waivers or sole-source justifications.
2. Vendor communications. All communications (email, text/SMS, letters, meeting notes, calendar invitations) between agency personnel and representatives of any vendor identified above (including the vendor's @flocksafety.com, @peregrine.io, or equivalent domains), concerning procurement, deployment, configuration, camera or sensor siting, pilot / early-access / free-trial programs, and any product beyond ALPR cameras.
3. Search and audit logs. The complete audit/usage logs showing each search or query, including — for Flock — the "Organization Audit" and "Network Audit" logs (Flock Insights dashboard), and — for any RTCC / data-integration platform (e.g., Peregrine) — the user access and query logs. For each entry, please include all available metadata fields, e.g.: record ID, user name, organization/agency name, date/time of search, license plate or query terms, stated reason, case number, camera count, time frame searched, filters, search type, and any text/AI prompt. Please export in the system's native machine-readable format (CSV/XLSX), not as a PDF printout, and do not strip metadata fields.
4. Hotlist and NCIC configuration (commonly the most important item). Records sufficient to show the full hotlist configuration of any ALPR system, including a screenshot, screen capture, printout, or CSV of the hotlists the agency subscribes to. This specifically includes which FBI NCIC "topics" are enabled and, in particular, whether the "Immigration Violator" file / topic is enabled, and the date any such topic was enabled or disabled. Also include any custom hotlists created by the agency.
5. Data sharing and external / federal access. A list of all external entities with which data is shared or from which it is received, and the settings governing that sharing, including:

The agency's Flock network-sharing settings, and whether "National Lookup" and/or statewide lookup are enabled, with the dates access was granted, modified, or revoked;
All external agencies that can access this agency's data, and all agencies whose data this agency can access, with dates;
Specifically, any access by or sharing with federal agencies — ICE, CBP, HSI, ATF, FBI, DHS — including records of searches those agencies (or other agencies on their behalf) ran against this agency's data;
All MOUs, data-sharing agreements, and network-participation terms (e.g., with a fusion center such as NCRIC), and any restrictions placed on downstream use or re-dissemination.

6. California ALPR statutory records (SB 34 and amendments).

The record of access required by Civil Code § 1798.90.52;
The agency's current ALPR usage and privacy policy required by Civil Code § 1798.90.51 (and, if the agency is an ALPR end-user, its policy under § 1798.90.53);
The results of the annual audit of ALPR searches for compliance with the usage/privacy policy (Civil Code § 1798.90.53), including any assessment of whether non-hotlist data was purged within 30 days of collection;
Any records concerning use of ALPR for immigration-enforcement geolocation or retention beyond 30 days (see Civ. Code § 1798.90.5 et seq., as amended).

7. Camera / sensor deployment and locations. Records sufficient to show the number, type, and locations of all cameras or sensors installed in the jurisdiction (fixed ALPR, mobile ALPR, PTZ/video, gunshot-detection, or other), their installation dates, and any encroachment, right-of-way, or other permits issued for their installation.
8. Data sources integrated into any data-integration / RTCC platform. For any platform identified above (e.g., Peregrine), a list of all data sources, feeds, and databases integrated into or accessible through the platform — for example computer-aided dispatch (CAD), records management systems (RMS), body-worn and in-car camera footage, fixed/traffic/school cameras, ALPR data, jail/booking data, DMV or state databases, and any third-party or commercial data sources — together with any system-configuration or data-source inventory documents.
9. Retention, governance, and training. Records reflecting data-retention periods and deletion practices, access controls (who is authorized to search and what approvals are required), prohibited uses, training materials, and internal policies, standard operating procedures, directives, or general orders governing use of any system identified above.
10. Misuse, breaches, and oversight. Any audits, reports, internal-affairs records, complaints, disciplinary records, or communications concerning suspected or confirmed misuse of any system (including searches for personal, immigration, or reproductive-health-related reasons), and any records of data breaches or security incidents involving the data.
11. Surveillance-use policy and impact reports. Any Surveillance Use Policy, Surveillance Impact Report, Privacy Impact Assessment / Data Protection Impact Assessment, or comparable document required by any applicable local surveillance-oversight ordinance, relating to ALPR, RTCC, or data-integration technology generally or to a specific vendor.
12. Governing-body review. Staff reports, resolutions, meeting agendas, minutes, and presentations to the city council / board of supervisors / oversight body concerning approval, funding, or renewal of any contract identified above.
13. Confirmation of non-use. If the agency has never used, piloted, or contracted for any ALPR, connected-camera, RTCC, or data-integration system of the kind described above, please confirm that in writing.

Format, preservation, and processing

Machine-readable format. Please provide records in their original electronic, machine-readable format with metadata intact (Gov. Code § 7922.570); spreadsheets and logs as CSV/XLSX, not PDF printouts.
Preservation. Because some responsive records (particularly ALPR search/audit logs) may be subject to short retention or automatic deletion, I request that the agency preserve all responsive records — and suspend any automatic purge of responsive audit logs — pending completion of this request.
Segregability and exemption log. If any record is withheld in whole or in part, please identify each record and the specific exemption claimed (Gov. Code § 7922.540), and release all reasonably segregable portions (Gov. Code § 7922.525). Data describing how the system operates and is used — as distinct from information about a specific individual — is generally not exempt investigative material (see ACLU of S. Cal. v. Superior Court (2017) 3 Cal.5th 1032). Personal information may be redacted while still disclosing system-level records.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 calendar days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Christian Whitney

communications.subject: RE: California Public Records Act Request: Flock Safety ALPR Records (Contracts, Audit Logs, SB 34, Communications)
communications.communication:
Thank you for the records produced on September 28 for PRA 26-446. I have downloaded the Dropbox materials.

Several items in my request were not addressed. The response did not produce records for them, state that none exist, or claim an exemption. Please provide a determination for each item below (Gov. Code § 7922.535). If any record is withheld in whole or in part, please identify the specific exemption relied on (Gov. Code § 7922.540).

Flock audit and sharing records (Items 3, 4 and 5)
Please produce the following for the City of Lakewood's Flock account, covering the period from when the first cameras went live in June 2025 through when the account was deactivated:
  1. The Organization Audit log (all searches run against Lakewood's cameras by authorized users);
  2. The Network Audit log (all searches of Lakewood's data by other agencies);
  3. The Event Log, or equivalent record, of changes to settings, including network sharing, National Lookup, statewide lookup and hotlists;
  4. The network sharing export or list of agencies granted access, with the dates access was granted and revoked;
  5. Screenshots or exports of the hotlist configuration.

These records exist and the City has used them. The March 24, 2026 staff report (p. 6) describes an audit of data sharing that "Staff, with the assistance of Flock, recently conducted." It found that 15 out-of-state agencies and the U.S. Postal Inspection Service were granted access between mid-June and September 15, 2025. City emails show that Director Yordt asked Flock for a network audit on March 4, 2026. On March 8, 2026, Flock reported that it had "sent over the logs from June–September 2025 to Sgt. Johnson." Please produce those logs and the audit described in the staff report.

Format: please produce each log exactly as exported from Flock, as CSV or XLSX files. Please do not produce PDFs or printouts, merge files, delete columns or rename files. If any field is redacted, please redact only that field's contents, keep all columns, and cite the exemption for each redacted field. I request the logs unredacted, including plate numbers, search reasons and case numbers. Please see ACLU of S. Cal. v. Superior Court (2017) 3 Cal.5th 1032 on releasing system-level ALPR records.

Preservation: because the Flock pilot has ended and the cameras have been removed, I ask that the City export these logs from Flock now, and notify Flock to preserve them, while the City still has access to the account.

If the City's position is that any of these records are held only by the Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department or by Flock, please say so for each item. The City signed the Flock agreement and has stated that it owns the data, so records it can obtain from Flock remain within its possession. Please also assist in locating them (Gov. Code § 7922.600).

REMAINING ITEMS
  • SB 34 records (Item 6): the § 1798.90.52 access records and the results of any § 1798.90.53 audits, including the monthly audits by Lakewood Station noted in the March 24, 2026 minutes. Please also produce the equivalent search and audit logs from the Vigilant/LEARN system for the City's cameras.
  • Training, SOPs, misuse and impact reports (Items 9–11): please produce these, or confirm in writing that none exist.
  • January 2020 – May 2023 (Items 1–2): the production begins in May 2023. Please produce earlier Vigilant/Motorola contracts and communications, or confirm that none exist.
  • Non-use (Item 13): please confirm whether the City has used Peregrine, Palantir, Fusus or a similar platform.

communications.subject: Response: Follow-Up Request: PRA 26-446 - Various Records Re Automated License Plate Readers; Whitney
communications.communication:
Good Afternoon:



Attached please find the record responsive to your follow-up request. Please note that the City contracts law enforcement services with the Los Angeles County Sheriff Department. The City of Lakewood does not have any additional records responsive to your request as the City does not have access to Flock Camera data.  Access and use of the Flock Camera system is restricted to law enforcement agency personnel only; City staff are not authorized users of the system.  Relative to the language included in the March 24, 2026, Staff Report, the City requested that Flock conduct a network audit of the system. The records generated by Flock as a result of the audit are attached. As a contract City with the Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department, only authorized personnel of the LASD would be able to access the data. You are encouraged to contact the Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department at Records & ID Bureau, 562-345-4441<tel:(562)%20345-4441>, to submit your records request.

Note that the PRA provides for the inspection or copying of existing identifiable public records; it does not compel the City to respond directly to questions, requests for information, or create new records, lists, or reports in response to a request.

The undersigned has made this determination upon the advice of the City Attorney's Office.
Sincerely,

communications.subject: Colorado Open Records Act Request: Chaffee Sheriff Office ALPR Audit History
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Colorado Open Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

Per the Chaffee County Sheriff's Office Policy Manual, Policy 426 ALPR: 

426.3 ALPR OPERATION
d. No member of this office shall operate ALPR equipment or access ALPR data without first completing office-approved training.
& 
426.5 ACCOUNTABILITY AND SAFEGUARDS
e. ALPR system audits should be conducted on a regular basis.

• Please provide all documents considered to be part of the "office-approved training"

• Please provide a list of system audits that have been conducted since Dec 1st, 2024

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 3 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

William Beckett

title: KING COUNTY DIRECTORS' ASSOCIATION – Board of Directors Meeting(s) Records (2022)

communications.subject: Washington Public Records Act Request: KING COUNTY DIRECTORS' ASSOCIATION – Board of Directors Meeting(s) Records (2022)
communications.communication:
KING COUNTY DIRECTORS' ASSOCIATION – Board of Directors Meeting(s) Records (2022)

June 04, 2026

via email to: Kristen Deskin, Human Resources Manager and Public Records Officer <kdeskin@kcda.org>

To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Washington Public Records Act [RCW 42.56], I hereby request the following records:

1. Produce copies of all "Records and Writings" of all minutes, complete meeting packets, resolutions, audio or video recordings, executive session logs, and presentations, inclusive, for every meeting of the KCDA Board of Directors for the year 2022, including all records provided to the Board by Executive Directors Bart Powelson or David Mahalko regarding litigation updates, vendor awards, or funding-out contract terminations.

DEFINITION OF RECORDS AND WRITINGS

"RECORDS AND WRITINGS" as defined by RCW 42.56.010(4): any handwriting, typewriting, printing, photostating, photographing, and every other means of recording any form of communication or representation including, but not limited to, letters, words, pictures, sounds, or symbols, or combination thereof, and all papers, maps, magnetic or paper tapes, photographic films and prints, motion picture, film and video recordings, magnetic or punched cards, discs, drums, diskettes, sound recordings, and other documents including existing data compilations from which information may be obtained or translated.

PRODUCTION PROCESSING AND DELIVERY OF ELECTRONIC RECORDS

Please provide all records in their native electronic format. Please do not instead create new records by printing electronic files then scanning and printing the newly scanned prints.

To preserve metadata and ease review, please produce as follows:

Emails: PST (Microsoft Outlook) or MBOX containers.

Chats/Texts/IM: Native exports where supported; otherwise, CSV/JSON with fields for sender, recipients, timestamps (UTC), message/thread IDs, and attachments (export attachments in original formats).

Calendars: ICS where possible; or PDF plus any attachments.

Documents/attachments: Original/native formats (DOCX, XLSX, PPTX, PDF, etc.).

Logs/Reports: CSV/JSON preferred.

Delivery: Direct electronic transmission via email attachments or open (no login/registration/password) download link hosted by your agency (e.g., SharePoint/OneDrive public link). Please do not use third-party portals that require creating an account or logging in. A single or series of .zip files is acceptable.

If any records cannot be produced in the above formats, please produce them in their native format with associated metadata intact.

METADATA REQUESTED

Where reasonably available, please include customary metadata fields such as: From, To, CC, BCC, Subject, Sent/Received Date-Time (with timezone/UTC), Message-ID, Conversation/Thread-ID, file names, file sizes, hash values (if held), and folder/location paths.

SEARCH DETAILS AND RECORDS PRESERVATION

Please identify the systems searched e.g. (Exchange/Outlook/Office 365, Teams, mobile devices, MDM archives, JustFOIA/CivicPlus admin, helpdesk, file shares) and the custodians.

Please describe the search methods/terms used.

If any potentially responsive sources were not searched or are no longer available, please explain why and what preservation steps were taken.

USE OF THIRD-PARTY PORTALS NOT MANDATORY

Please note that under Washington’s Public Records Act, use of a third-party “portal” is not mandatory for requestors. Agencies may not condition access to records on the creation of an account, the use of a login, or the acceptance of third-party vendor terms.

Third-party portals (such as GovQA, NextRequest, JustFOIA, or similar systems) often:

Require account creation or login credentials;

Restrict downloads, viewing times, or re-access;

Remove or disable links after a limited period;

Place records behind commercial platforms operated by for-profit corporations.

These restrictions unlawfully burden and condition access to public records. The Public Records Act forbids agencies from imposing access barriers beyond those authorized by statute.

RCW 42.56.080(2): An agency “shall not deny a request for identifiable public records solely on the basis that the request is overbroad.” Agencies must provide the “fullest assistance” and “most timely possible action” to requestors.

RCW 42.56.550(1): Courts are directed to liberally construe the PRA to ensure access and strictly construe exemptions against withholding.

Fisher Broadcasting-Seattle TV LLC v. City of Seattle, 180 Wn.2d 515, 528 (2014): Agencies must produce records in a “reasonably usable format when feasible.”

Mechling v. City of Monroe, 152 Wn. App. 830, 841 (2009): PRA is to be liberally construed in favor of disclosure and cannot be restricted by agency practices.

Because of this, I respectfully decline use of any third-party portal. Please provide all responsive records via:

Direct electronic email attachment to this requestor’s address, or a direct, open (no password, no registration required) cloud-based download link hosted by your agency.

Do not register this requestor with, nor direct this requestor to, any third-party commercial portal, including but not limited to FOIAOnline, GovQA (a Granicus Corporation), NextRequest, FOIAExpress, JustFOIA, FOIADirect, or any similar online service.

Do not transmit any portion of this request, or responsive records, to any for-profit vendor or portal. Doing so would unlawfully condition access to public records and contravene both RCW 42.56.080 and RCW 42.56.550.

PUBLIC RECORDS REQUESTS SUBMITTED VIA EMAIL

This public records request is being submitted via email, consistent with Washington’s Public Records Act.

RCW 42.56.080(2) provides in relevant part: “Agencies shall honor requests received in person during an agency’s normal office hours, or by mail or email, for identifiable public records unless exempted by provisions of this chapter. No official format is required for making a records request; however, agencies may recommend that requestors submit requests using an agency-provided form or web page.”

Accordingly:

A request submitted by email is a valid, enforceable method of making a PRA request.

Agencies may recommend, but cannot require, the use of an online portal or official form.

Any refusal to honor this request as submitted would directly conflict with RCW 42.56.080 and the agency’s duty under RCW 42.56.100 to provide the “fullest assistance to requestors” and adopt reasonable rules that do not “unreasonably hinder or delay” access.

Therefore, this request is to be honored and fulfilled by your agency via email, as submitted. Should the agency fail to process this request in compliance with statute, relief will be sought pursuant to RCW 42.56.550 in the form of judicial review, penalties, and attorney’s fees.

INSTALLMENTS AND FEE ESTIMATES

Please provide an initial acknowledgment within five business days (RCW 42.56.520) with a reasonable time estimate for each installment, and

A cost estimate if fees are anticipated (please itemize and explain).

NISSEN AFFIDAVIT AND ALL DEVICE SEARCH REQUIRED

Pursuant to Nissen v. Pierce County, 183 Wn.2d 863 (2015), and its progeny, this request specifically includes all responsive public records contained on personal devices or personal accounts (including personal cell phones, text/SMS/MMS, personal email accounts, cloud storage, instant messaging apps, and social media accounts) of any agency employee, official, or contractor where public business may have been conducted.

To comply with this requirement, please:

Conduct a comprehensive all-device search, including both agency-issued and personally owned devices/accounts used for public business.

Require each potentially responsive custodian to execute a Nissen affidavit or sworn certification affirming:

1. They conducted a diligent search of all personal and agency devices/accounts reasonably likely to contain responsive records;

2. The methods used to conduct the search (e.g., search terms, accounts checked, device types); and

3. Whether any responsive records were located, preserved, and produced.

Produce all responsive records located in such searches along with the executed affidavits.

Failure to obtain and provide sworn Nissen affidavits or equivalent certifications from custodians may constitute an incomplete search in violation of RCW 42.56.520 (requirement for a reasonable and adequate search) and may expose the agency to relief under RCW 42.56.550.

EXEMPTION LOGS 

Please ensure that all redactions or exemptions claimed by your agency in the production of responsive records are accompanied by a complete and detailed exemption log.

Exemptions logs at minimum must contain the following:

1. Identify the valid legal reason (statutory citation) for each exemption;

2. Specify the location of each redaction within the record produced (via footnote, coded reference, or margin notation);

3. State the number of pages or records withheld in their entirety, if any; and

4. Demonstrate that only the minimal exempt portion of any record has been withheld, as required by law.

The Washington Public Records Act requires agencies to justify each withholding or redaction:

RCW 42.56.210(3): “Agency responses refusing, in whole or in part, inspection of any public record shall include a statement of the specific exemption authorizing the withholding of the record (or part) and a brief explanation of how the exemption applies to the record withheld.”

RCW 42.56.210(1): Exemptions must be narrowly construed.

Washington courts have repeatedly enforced this duty:

Rental Housing Ass’n of Puget Sound v. City of Des Moines, 165 Wn.2d 525, 538 (2009): Agencies must provide specific explanations for each exemption; conclusory or vague justifications are insufficient.

Sanders v. State, 169 Wn.2d 827, 845 (2010): “The burden of proof is on the agency to establish that refusal to permit public inspection and copying is in accordance with a statute.”

Resident Action Council v. Seattle Housing Auth., 177 Wn.2d 417, 433 (2013): Agencies must disclose the non-exempt portions of records and cannot withhold more than necessary.

Therefore, I request that your agency provide an itemized exemption log with each installment of records produced, in compliance with RCW 42.56.210(3) and the above case law, ensuring transparency and accountability in the redaction process.

COMMERCIAL PURPOSE DECLARATION

This public records request is not being made for any commercial purpose. The Washington State Public Records Act (PRA) prohibits agencies from disclosing “lists of individuals” for commercial purposes.

RCW 42.56.070(8) states: “This chapter shall not be construed as giving authority to any agency to give, sell, or provide access to lists of individuals requested for commercial purposes….”

Accordingly:

This request does not seek a “list of individuals.”

This request is not made for any commercial purpose.

This declaration satisfies all requirements of RCW 42.56.070(8) regarding prohibitions on lists and commercial purposes.

Warning: The PRA does not authorize agencies to require requestors to complete additional “commercial purpose declarations” when the request does not seek a list of individuals. Such requirements improperly condition access to public records in violation of RCW 42.56.080(2) (requests must be honored by mail or email, no official format required) and RCW 42.56.100 (agencies must provide the fullest assistance to requestors and may not adopt rules that unreasonably hinder or delay access).

Washington courts have consistently rejected agency attempts to impose conditions not found in statute:

Mechling v. City of Monroe, 152 Wn. App. 830, 841 (2009): The PRA is a strongly worded mandate for broad disclosure; agencies cannot erect unauthorized barriers.

SEIU Local 925 v. University of Washington, 193 Wn.2d 860, 875 (2019): The PRA is to be liberally construed to promote access, and exemptions must be narrowly applied.

Therefore, no additional commercial purpose declaration will be completed for this request. Any attempt to impose such a requirement would be an unlawful restriction of rights under RCW 42.56.

PRESERVATION OF PUBLIC RECORDS *** ANTICIPATE LITIGATION *** WAC 44-14-03005 RETENTION OF PUBLIC RECORDS

WAC 44-14-03005 (Retention of Public Records) makes clear that public records are subject to retention schedules, and that unlawful destruction can constitute a crime.

RCW 40.16.010 and RCW 40.16.020 criminalize the unlawful mutilation, destruction, or concealment of public records.

RCW 42.56.100 expressly prohibits an agency from destroying any public record after a public records request has been made for that record, even if the record would otherwise be scheduled for lawful destruction.

In addition, agencies have heightened retention obligations when litigation is reasonably anticipated. Records potentially relevant to actual or anticipated litigation must be preserved until both the public records request and the litigation have been fully resolved.

Legal Consequences of Premature Destruction: In Yacobellis v. City of Bellingham, 55 Wn. App. 706, 780 P.2d 272 (1989), the Court of Appeals held that an agency violates the Public Records Act and is subject to attorneys’ fees and statutory penalties when it destroys responsive records after receiving a public records request.

By contrast, it is not a PRA violation if a record was destroyed prior to the agency’s receipt of a request, provided the destruction was lawful under retention schedules. See Bldg. Indus. Ass’n of Wash. v. McCarthy, 152 Wn. App. 720, 218 P.3d 196 (2009); West v. Dep’t of Natural Resources, 163 Wn. App. 238, 258 P.3d 78 (2011).

Washington courts have emphasized that the Public Records Act (RCW 42.56) and the state’s records retention laws (RCW 40.14) are separate but complementary. Agencies must comply with both.

Accordingly:

Your agency must preserve all potentially responsive records immediately upon receipt of this request.

No responsive records may be altered, deleted, or destroyed until this request has been fully resolved and any related litigation constraints have been lifted.

Any unlawful destruction of responsive records may expose the agency and its officials to criminal liability (RCW 40.16), civil penalties, and mandatory attorneys’ fees (RCW 42.56.550(4)).

RECORDS INSTALLMENTS - ORDER OF PRODUCTION

If production of responsive records will be completed in multiple installments, production in reverse chronological order is strongly preferred to the extent supported by native system exports, provided it does not delay the delivery of installments.

DIGITAL COMPRESSION AND FILE MINIMIZATION REQUESTED IN ACCORDANCE WITH RCW 42.56

Pursuant to RCW 42.56.080(2), please provide all responsive electronic records in the fewest number of individual files, preserving native formats wherever possible. Where appropriate, please use free digital compression (.zip or equivalent) to consolidate responsive records into the smallest number of installments for efficiency and economy.

This approach reduces agency burden, promotes prompt disclosure, and minimizes potential costs to the requestor, consistent with the Public Records Act’s directive that agencies provide records in the most “reasonably locatable form” and “fullest assistance to requestors.” See RCW 42.56.100 (agency duty to adopt reasonable rules for providing fullest assistance); RCW 42.56.120(2)(b) (fees must reflect actual costs, not used to discourage access).

Washington courts have consistently held that agencies must facilitate access in a practical, non-burdensome manner. See Fisher Broadcasting-Seattle TV LLC v. City of Seattle, 180 Wn.2d 515, 528 (2014) (agencies must provide records in a usable format when reasonably feasible); Mechling v. City of Monroe, 152 Wn. App. 830, 841 (2009) (PRA is to be liberally construed in favor of disclosure). Producing consolidated, digitally compressed files satisfies these obligations by reducing unnecessary fragmentation and excess per-page charges.

Accordingly, I request that each installment be produced as a single compressed .zip file (or as few as technically necessary), containing all responsive records in native format, to ensure both compliance with RCW 42.56 and an economical calculation of any applicable public records fees.

COMMUNICATION VIA EMAIL

Please send all requests for clarification, status updates, and production of responsive electronic documents via direct email reply.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. We look forward to receiving your response to this request within 5 business days, as the statute requires.

Good Luck.

RE: Response to Clarification Request, Board of Directors Meeting Records for 2022, request of June 4, 2026

Ms. Bradford,

This responds to KCDA's July 12 clarification request. The request seeks two categories of records, both limited to calendar year 2022.

First, the enumerated meeting record categories: all minutes, complete meeting packets, resolutions, audio or video recordings, executive session logs, and presentations, for every meeting of the KCDA Board of Directors. Complete meeting packets means the full set of materials distributed to board members for each meeting, including every attachment, report, and exhibit distributed with the packet.

Second, all records provided to the Board by Executive Directors Bart Powelson or David Mahalko regarding litigation updates, vendor awards, or funding-out contract terminations, in whatever form those records exist. If such a record was provided to the Board by email, the transmitting email and its attachments are responsive records.

Third, within both categories above, RECORDS AND WRITINGS carries the full definition stated in the original public records request, as defined by RCW 42.56.010(4): any handwriting, typewriting, printing, photostating, photographing, and every other means of recording any form of communication or representation including, but not limited to, letters, words, pictures, sounds, or symbols, or combination thereof, and all papers, maps, magnetic or paper tapes, photographic films and prints, motion picture, film and video recordings, magnetic or punched cards, discs, drums, diskettes, sound recordings, and other documents including existing data compilations from which information may be obtained or translated. A record falling within either category above is responsive regardless of its medium, form, or storage format, and no such record may be excluded on the ground that it is a recording, a note, an electronic file, or a data compilation rather than a paper document.

To be clear as to the question KCDA asked: the clarification KCDA seeks concerns subject matter, and the answer is that the request does not seek KCDA's general electronic correspondence beyond the records described above. The definition above concerns form, and no record within the two categories described above is outside the request because of its form.

With scope now confirmed, please note the enumerated categories are discrete records for a closed calendar year, maintained in the ordinary course of business. KCDA's July 10 first installment contained two records, the August and October 2022 minutes. Please state, as an actual calendar date, when KCDA will produce the remaining 2022 minutes, meeting packets, and resolutions, and provide the installment schedule for the balance of the request.

My June 29 and July 10 requests regarding fees also stand. If KCDA anticipates any charge for any future installment, please provide, pursuant to RCW 42.56.120(2)(f) and before any copies are made, a summary of the applicable charges, stating the fee schedule relied upon, the per unit rate, the units counted, and the total estimated fee, so that I may revise the request to reduce any charges.

Please list every 2022 board meeting, state which meetings' minutes, complete packets, and resolutions remain unproduced, and state the actual calendar date on which each remaining installment will be produced. A single completion date of September 4, 2026 is not an installment schedule, and these are discrete, compiled records for a closed calendar year.
  
2. Recordings and executive session logs. For the third time: if no audio or video recordings exist for any 2022 board meeting, or if no executive session logs exist, please say so plainly. If they exist, please state when they will be produced. Leaving a requested category unaddressed in three consecutive responses is a response in itself, and it is being recorded as one.
  
3. The fee summary, before copies are made. Your July 15 email states that fees "will be calculated consistent with its policy and RCW 42.56.120, and explained in correspondence from KCDA." RCW 42.56.120(2)(f) runs the other way: a requestor may ask, and "if requested an agency shall provide," a summary of the applicable charges before any copies are made, so the request can be revised to reduce them. I asked on June 29, on July 10, and on July 13. Please provide, now and before any charged installment is prepared: the fee schedule provision relied upon, the per-unit rate, the units to be counted, what each counted unit consists of, the total estimated fee, and the arithmetic. If KCDA declines to provide the summary in advance, please say so plainly.
  

This request is not abandoned and will not be abandoned. Nothing in this correspondence waives, limits, or releases any right or remedy.

Thank you
