communications.communication:
RE: REQUEST FOR CLARIFICATION

08-06-2026

Via Email to: andrea.bradford@foster.com

Ms. Bradford,

Attached is the original public records request.

Please produce records responsive to this request, not other requests.

1. The request.

The attached request, submitted June 4, 2026, seeks all minutes, complete meeting packets, resolutions, audio or video recordings, executive session logs, and presentations, inclusive, for every meeting of the KCDA Board of Directors for the year 2022, including all records provided to the Board by Executive Directors Bart Powelson or David Mahalko regarding litigation updates, vendor awards, or funding-out contract terminations.

2. Outstanding on this request.

a. State which records are responsive to this request. I have no way of determining which of the records KCDA has transmitted are responsive to this request. Please state, by document title and date, the complete list of records KCDA contends are responsive to this request, identifying which of those records KCDA has already produced and which remain to be produced.

b. State any change to that list. If KCDA has previously identified a record as responsive to this request and no longer does, or now identifies as responsive a record it did not previously identify, state which record, state the change, and state the date KCDA made it.

c. Produce the complete meeting packets, resolutions, audio or video recordings, executive session logs, and presentations for every 2022 meeting. To date KCDA has produced minutes only. Every other category named in the request remains outstanding.

d. Produce the records provided to the Board by Executive Directors Bart Powelson or David Mahalko regarding litigation updates, vendor awards, or funding-out contract terminations. KCDA has produced nothing responsive to this part of the request and has not addressed it.

e. Provide a contemporaneous exemption log with each installment, identifying each record or portion withheld or redacted, the specific exemption claimed, and a brief explanation of how it applies to the particular record. RCW 42.56.210(3). No log has been provided with any installment on this request.

f. Provide the summary of applicable charges required by RCW 42.56.120(2)(f) for the complete response to this request, before any charges are incurred: the total estimated number of responsive records and pages, the per unit rate, the statutory or adopted schedule authority for that rate, the number of units, and the total estimated charge. A link to KCDA's policy is not that summary.

g. Provide a reasonable estimate of the time required to respond stated as the calendar date of each installment between now and completion, not a single completion date. RCW 42.56.520(1)(c); WAC 44-14-04003(7). This has been requested in writing on June 29, July 10 and July 20, 2026 and has not been provided.

h. Produce the balance of the 2022 records. KCDA produced two documents on July 10, 2026 as a first installment for a full closed calendar year. Nothing further has been produced in the twenty-seven days since.

i. State whether any audio or video recording of any 2022 Board of Directors meeting exists in KCDA's possession, custody or control. KCDA's July 24, 2026 statement that "KCDA does not record board meetings" does not state whether a recording of any 2022 meeting exists. If none exists, state that. If any exists, identify the meetings.

j. Identify the 2022 Board of Directors meetings for which KCDA has located responsive records, and the meetings for which it has located none. KCDA declined this on July 24, 2026, citing WAC 44-14-04002(2). Identifying which meetings are covered by a production is not an interrogatory; it is a statement of what the agency has produced and what it has not.

k. KCDA's July 12, 2026 message asks whether this request seeks electronic communications or only the enumerated record types. The request states what it seeks and the attached copy is the answer. Produce all records responsive to the request as written.

l. KCDA stated on July 24, 2026 that it "does not have a total cost estimate at this time." Where a requestor challenges the reasonableness of an agency's estimate, the burden of showing it reasonable rests with the agency. RCW 42.56.520(2).

If KCDA contends at any point that this request has been abandoned, KCDA must say so in writing before it closes anything, identifying the installment it relies on, the date it contends the period began, the date it contends the period ended, and the records it relies on for the contention. I am entitled to answer that contention before the request is closed rather than after.

Nothing in this reply should be read as agreement that any charge is owing, or as an agreement to any date.

This request is not abandoned and will not be abandoned. Nothing in this correspondence waives, limits, or releases any right or remedy.

Thank you.

communications.subject: RE: [EXTERNAL] Colorado Open Records Act Request: Denver Police Department Axon Requests (Denver Police Department)
communications.communication:
Good afternoon –
Following a good faith search, please see the attached records responsive to your request available to the public. Records of the Denver Police Department are criminal justice records, the disclosure of which is governed by the Colorado Criminal Justice Records Act (CCJRA), sections 24-72-301, et. seq. C.R.S.  Except for records of “official actions,” the disclosure of criminal justice records is discretionary and can be denied where the custodian believes disclosure would be contrary to the public interest. Section 24-72-305(5), C.R.S.
 Pursuant to Harris v. Denver Post, 123 P.3d 116 (Colo. 2005), the following factors , in addition to other relevant considerations,  may be used to determine whether a record should be released or withheld:

  1.  the privacy interests of individuals, if any, who may be impacted by a decision to allow disclosure of the record;
  2.  the agency’s interest in keeping confidential information confidential;
  3.  the agency’s interest in the integrity of on-going investigations;
  4.  the public purpose to be served in allowing disclosure of the record; and
  5.  any other pertinent considerations relevant to the circumstances of the records request, including whether disclosure would be contrary to the public interest.
Based upon my consideration of the relevant factors, I have determined that certain information should be redacted from the report prior to public disclosure to protect privacy and interests which outweigh the public interest in disclosure of the information.  The redacted columns include, names of officers, case numbers, time frame, license plate information, filters (which included case numbers and other information related to criminal investigation)s) and entries from within the reason column have been redacted.
We also want to proactively share some important context with you regarding two entries in the May audit log.

The two queries on May 19, 2026, with the offense category listed as “Other; Immigration Violator” were test queries submitted by Denver Police personnel during DPD’s testing phase conducted prior to the go-live date of June 3, 2026, for its Axon ALPR pilot program. More specifically, the queries were submitted to see if the system would allow such a query and how it would be reported in the audit so that DPD could provide feedback to the vendor. So, to be clear, these two queries were submitted for the purpose of testing the system prior to implementation and were not submitted for the purpose of any enforcement.
In accordance with Denver municipal ordinance and Colorado law, the Denver Police Department does not assist with the enforcement of civil federal immigration laws.
Thank you,
Andrea

communications.subject: RE: North Carolina Public Records Law Request: Untitled
communications.communication:
Good afternoon,

The North Carolina Administrative Office of the Courts (NCAOC) is in receipt of your public records request.  Bulk data extracts and real-time access to data are available through the NCAOC's remote public access (RPA) program, which is intended to be the "sole means of remote electronic access" to compilations of electronic court records under G.S. 7A-109(d).  LexisNexis Risk Data Mgmt. v. N.C. Admin. Office of the Courts, 368 N.C. 180, 187-88 (2015).  This level of public access is consistent with the Public Records Act and G.S. 7A-109(d).  See, e.g., G.S. §§ 7A-109(d), 132- 6.1(a1).  You can learn more about the NCAOC Remote Public Access Program at: https://www.nccourts.gov/services/remote-public-access-program/rpa-online-access and at https://www.nccourts.gov/services/remote-public-access-program.  As explained on the website, participation in the RPA program requires a signed licensing agreement, a performance bond, and payment for the various extracts.

Non-confidential data contained in the ACIS Historical Demographic Extract is also available in the individual criminal case records available to the public for free through the eCourts Portal (https://portal-nc.tylertech.cloud/Portal/); please visit Portal to review these records.

Thank you for your inquiry.

publicrecords@nccourts.org<mailto:publicrecords@nccourts.org>

website: nccourts.gov<http://nccourts.gov/>

title: Dolly Parton

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: Dolly Parton
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

Records mentioning, relating to, or generated as a result of investigation or inquiry into musician Dolly Rebecca Parton Dean (January 19, 1946 – August 25, 2026). Her death is widely-known and widely reported; as such, privacy concerns under FOIA Exemptions 6 and 7 are voided, as are any concerns under the Privacy Act. For example, you may find her New York Times obituary at the following link: https://www.nytimes.com/2026/08/25/arts/music/dolly-parton-dead.html

Please conduct a search of the Central Records System, including but not limited to the Electronic Surveillance (ELSUR) Indices, the Microphone Surveillance (MISUR) Indices, the Physical Surveillance (FISUR) Indices, and the Technical Surveillance (TESUR) Indices, for both main-file records and cross-reference records of both HQ and all field offices for all relevant names, agencies, organizations, companies and events including but not limited to those cited in the previous paragraphs and/or links as well as a cross-reference with the Southern Poverty Law Center to include any information provided by the SPLC. My request includes but is not limited to 137, 157, 176, 177, 183, 184, 188, and 214 files. If previously released records are available, then I request a rolling release consisting of those records while additional records are located and processed for release.

If any part of these documents are exempt from disclosure, please be sure to review and release all reasonably segregable nonexempt portions of responsive documents, as the FOIA requires.

I request that I be properly classified as a media requester. I am an assistant editor at Reason Magazine who has written numerous articles on topics of public interest, and I am requesting these documents in an editorial capacity. Please contact me if you have any questions about my media status.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Matthew Petti

communications.subject: California Public Records Act Request: CPRA - Ventura County - Flock Safety Documents (Ventura Police Department)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the California Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

- Organization Audit in Flock. 
All data logged from July 1, 2023 to the date this request is processed. Per Flock's documentation, this report is available within the Insights tab and reflects searches conducted within the agency.

- Network Audit in Flock. 
All data logged from July 1, 2023 to the date this request is processed. Per Flock's documentation, this report is available within the Insights tab and reflects searches of the agency's Flock network by any agency in the Flock system.

- Hardware.
The current number and installed locations of any Flock Safety, LPR,  AVIS, or machine learning-assisted camera systems (provide locations as coordinates or address with nearest cross-street), and any documents related to planned future installations of the same.

- Documents.
>  Invoices, contracts, purchase orders, and bid documents related to the acquisition or renewal of Flock Safety products or services
>  Agreements with homeowner associations, private businesses, or individuals for access to Flock Safety systems
>  Training materials, policies, and SOPs related to Flock Safety platform use
>  Grant or funding records related to the Flock system
>  Data retention policies for data collected by Flock Safety systems
>  Any complaints or grievances received from the public regarding ALPR camera placement or data use


I am not requesting personally identifiable information or license plate data. If any responsive record contains such information, please redact only that portion and produce the remainder. If any records are withheld, please provide a written index identifying each withheld record and the statutory exemption claimed.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 calendar days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Jordan
